editorial:
You follow police officer Cui Xun as he spends more than fifty years chasing dangerous cases and protecting ordinary people. The story moves through changing times, old streets, busy stations, and new technology, but the heart stays on Cui and his team doing hard, patient work. It feels like a long, steady ride with real stakes, not just flashy chases. You see him grow older while his sense of duty stays strong, and the cases connect to bigger changes around him. The mood is serious but warm, with moments of teamwork, tired humor, and quiet pride.

The acting feels natural, especially in scenes where Cui talks with victims or younger officers. Action is grounded, pacing is patient, and the big cases build slowly. Some stretches may feel long if you want fast twists, and the message can get heavy. Still, it rewards patient viewers who enjoy character-driven crime stories. If you like true-life police dramas, this is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Cui reopens one old case that has followed him for decades. He learns a trusted colleague hid evidence years ago to protect a powerful figure. Instead of looking away, Cui makes the arrest and closes the file. Afterward, he retires and hands his badge to a younger officer. The last shot shows the old case box sealed, with the city moving forward as a new generation takes over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true-crime police dramas and character stories.
